themes_detail.label: Park Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints from parks in CD310 spiked to 5 complaints THIS WEEK, a 900% increase versus the 0.5-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.5), suggesting a new pattern of disturbances or events in neighborhood parks.
evidence: 5 park noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.5)
900% spike is statistically significant and marks a clear departure from baseline
No Reddit or local news mentions yet, suggesting story is emerging before media coverage
reporting_angles: Which parks are generating complaints (Shore Road, Dyker Beach, etc.) and what activities are drivers?
Has there been a change in park programming, events, or hours that coincides with spike?

themes_detail.label: Abandoned Bikes Piling Up
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned bike complaints in CD310 surged to 6 reports last week, a 500% spike above the 1.0-complaint weekly baseline (z-score: 7.07), suggesting a new accumulation problem or organized dumping of bicycles.
evidence: 6 abandoned bike complaints last week vs. 1.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 7.07)
500% increase is one of the most statistically extreme spikes in the dataset
Correlates with broader illegal dumping spike (13 complaints last week, +121% vs baseline)
reporting_angles: Are bikes concentrated in specific locations (transit hubs, waterfront, residential blocks)?
Is this linked to e-bike or Citibike overstocking or a dumping hotspot?

themes_detail.label: Illegal Dumping & Litter Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Illegal dumping complaints hit 13 last week, up 121% from the 5.9-complaint weekly average (z-score: 3.63), and litter basket requests reached 3 complaints last week, a 500% spike from 0.5 weekly baseline (z-score: 3.54), indicating accelerating waste management failures.
evidence: 13 illegal dumping complaints last week vs. 5.9 weekly average (z-score: 3.63, +121%)
3 litter basket requests last week vs. 0.5 weekly average (z-score: 3.54, +500%)
Converges with long-standing CB budget request for 'garbage collection and recycling infrastructure'
Aligns with abandoned bikes spike—suggests broader debris/waste accumulation problem
reporting_angles: Where are illegal dumping sites concentrated and how long have they persisted?
Is this a Sanitation Department staffing/collection shortage or residents exploiting inadequate bin infrastructure?

themes_detail.label: Electrical & Street Light Failures
themes_detail.summary: Street light condition complaints peaked 3 weeks ago at 29 reports (128% above the 12.8-complaint weekly average, z-score: 5.22), and electrical complaints spiked to 5 reports 3 weeks ago (471% above 0.9 weekly average, z-score: 5.28), indicating a potential infrastructure breakdown or repair backlog.
evidence: 29 street light complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 12.8 weekly average (z-score: 5.22, +128%)
5 electrical complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.9 weekly average (z-score: 5.28, +471%)
Both spikes occurred in the same timeframe, suggesting a coordinated infrastructure event or outage
Correlates with CB request for 'DOB capital budget' improvements
reporting_angles: Did a storm, power outage, or Con Edison work cause the spike 3 weeks ago?
What is the current status of street light repairs and how long are residents waiting?

themes_detail.label: Outside Building Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Outside building condition complaints hit 3 reports 3 weeks ago, a 500% increase from the 0.5-complaint weekly baseline (z-score: 3.54), potentially signaling facade damage, exterior deterioration, or a specific building crisis.
evidence: 3 outside building complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.5 weekly average (z-score: 3.54, +500%)
Vague complaint category; unclear if tied to specific buildings or widespread issue
Correlates with 439 DOB filings in last 90 days (376 alterations, 21 new buildings, 14 demolitions)
reporting_angles: Which buildings triggered complaints and what exterior issues were reported?
Is this tied to active construction or weather-related damage?
